cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: to introduce the topic and clarify key target vocabulary for the session.

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Review the key vocabulary for this session below:

cosy-blockquote.p: ocean – a very large expanse of sea, in particular, each of the main areas of saline water.

p.em: Example: The vast blue ocean stretched as far as the eye could see.

cosy-blockquote.p: lifeboat – a small boat kept on a ship for use in an emergency.

p.em: Example: The ship was equipped with enough lifeboats for everyone on board.

cosy-blockquote.p: sink – go down below the surface of something, especially in liquid.

p.em: Example: The heavy iron anchor will sink quickly to the bottom of the sea.

cosy-blockquote.p: captain – the person in command of a ship, aircraft, or team.

p.em: Example: The experienced captain guided the ship safely through the storm.

cosy-blockquote.p: weakest – lacking physical strength or resolve; the least strong.

p.em: Example: We must protect and support the weakest members of our community.

cosy-blockquote.p: fighting – the action of defeating or resisting something; struggling.

p.em: Example: Fighting for social justice requires courage and perseverance.

cosy-blockquote.p: storm – a violent disturbance of the atmosphere with strong winds and rain.

p.em: Example: The loud thunder and lightning of the storm woke me up.

cosy-blockquote.p: wrong – not correct or true; incorrect.

p.em: Example: He gave the wrong answer to the simple physics question.

cosy-blockquote.p: outfit – a set of clothes worn together, typically for a particular occasion.

p.em: Example: She picked out a beautiful and stylish outfit for the wedding.

cosy-blockquote.p: crowded – full of people, leaving little or no room.

p.em: Example: The popular beach was very crowded on the warm summer weekend.

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Share whether you agree or disagree with these statements and discuss them with your teacher:

ul.li: Incorrect: There is a big improvement of → Correct: There is a big improvement in my English ((Use 'in' after 'improvement' to express domain.))
Incorrect: It was a great relief of → Correct: It was a great relief to hear the news ((Use 'relief' + infinitive 'to hear'.))
Incorrect: She is in the choir since → Correct: She has been in the choir for three years ((Use present perfect + 'for' to show duration of state.))
